_comment: The schema of the okf_check: block in okf-base.yaml. okf-verify enforces it (okf-verify --check-config) and okf-check calls that, so the two tools cannot disagree. A node is {keys: {name: node}} (a mapping with exactly those keys), {map: node} (a mapping with free non-empty string keys, each value a node), {list: node} (a list whose items are node), {enum: [values]} (one of those strings), {type: boolean} (true or false), {type: number, min, max, default} (a number within min..max; default is the value used when the key is absent), {type: integer, min, max} (a whole number within min..max; default is the value used when the key is absent) or {type: string} (a non-empty string). A node under keys may add {requires: {sibling: value}}: the key is only valid when that sibling has that value; or {below: sibling}: when that sibling is set, the value is smaller than it. A map node may add {key_no_prefix: !}: no key may start with that text. A list node may add {item_no_prefix: !}: no item may start with that text, and {min: N}: at least N items. A keys node may add {required: [names]}: those keys must be present. {type: regex} is a non-empty string that compiles as a Python regular expression with at least one capture group. To add an option, add its key under the top-level keys.

facts._comment: okf-knowledge-gate#15: each fact has a value and the patterns that find where it is stated (group 1 is the stated value); source names the note where the value is decided.

duplicates._comment: threshold 1.0: on the labelled sample (101 pairs, agent-labelled) no description overlap below 1.0 reached precision 0.8. body_threshold 0.6: on the 24 live body pairs of one vault, blind-labelled, 0.3 had precision 0.50 and 0.6 had 1.00 (every NOT at or below 0.57). time_limit in seconds.
